history.hpi: 48-year-old female at work reports sudden onset of palpitations and lightheadedness approximately 10 minutes prior to EMS arrival while seated at her desk. No preceding chest pain, exertion, or trauma. Denies prior similar episodes. Coworkers report she became pale, diaphoretic, and increasingly confused over the last few minutes before EMS arrival.
history.lastOralIntake: Coffee (approximately 2 cups) roughly 1 hour prior to onset; no solid food since breakfast
history.events: Sudden onset of palpitations and lightheadedness at her desk; coworker called 911 after noting she became pale, diaphoretic, and confused

scene.dispatch: 48-year-old female, difficulty breathing and dizziness, office building
scene.location: Third-floor office break room, downtown office building
scene.safety: Scene safe; coworkers present and cooperative, no hazards noted
scene.bystanders: Coworker reports sudden onset of palpitations approximately 10 minutes prior to EMS arrival; states patient became pale, diaphoretic, and confused shortly before crews arrived
visualCues: Patient seated in office chair, pale and diaphoretic
Patient clutching chest, appears anxious and disoriented

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: 48-year-old female found seated, pale, diaphoretic, and confused with a rapid, regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 210 and hypotension. Crew must rapidly recognize unstable SVT and prepare for definitive treatment.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Tachypneic, RR 22, mild accessory muscle use
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Rapid, thready radial pulse; delayed capillary refill ~3 seconds
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities, follows simple commands intermittently
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: My heart is racing... I feel really dizzy... (repeats questions, appears confused)

expectedActions.shortAction: Manage airway; administer O2 to target SpO2 94–98%
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Manage airway as necessary Administer oxygen as appropriate with a target of achieving 94–98% saturation
expectedActions.rationale: Ensures adequate oxygenation before further hemodynamic evaluation and treatment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Initiate cardiac monitoring and obtain 12-lead EKG
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms regular narrow-complex tachycardia and guides the treatment pathway.
Required for adenosine administration and preparation for possible sedation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Check blood glucose (obtained 98 mg/dL, rules out hypoglycemia as a contributing cause)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Check blood glucose and treat hypoglycemia per the Hypoglycemia Guideline
expectedActions.rationale: Hypoglycemia is a reversible cause of tachycardia and altered mental status that must be excluded.

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize hemodynamic instability (BP 78/50, altered mentation) as unstable SVT; prepare for synchronized cardioversion
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Regular Narrow Complex Tachycardia – Unstable: Deliver a synchronized shock based on manufacturer's recommendations.
expectedActions.rationale: Instability with hypotension and AMS mandates the unstable pathway and prompt preparation for cardioversion.

expectedActions.shortAction: Attempt vagal maneuvers (e.g., modified Valsalva) while preparing for cardioversion
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Regular Narrow Complex Tachycardia – Stable (SVT): Perform vagal maneuvers
expectedActions.rationale: A brief vagal maneuver attempt is reasonable while equipment for cardioversion and adenosine are prepared, without delaying definitive treatment.

transitions.condition: Crew performs vagal maneuvers (e.g., modified Valsalva) while continuing to prepare for possible cardioversion; the SVT persists unchanged.

phases.name: Vagal maneuvers attempted
phases.description: Vagal maneuvers performed without conversion; SVT persists with continued hypotension and worsening mentation. Adenosine is given as a bridge while cardioversion is prepared.
phases.triggerCondition: After a modified Valsalva maneuver, the rhythm remains unchanged at HR ~208 with continued hypotension (BP 76/48) and worsening confusion; adenosine is given per protocol while defibrillator pads and sedation are prepared for possible cardioversion.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Weak, thready pulse; capillary refill >3 seconds
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Confused mumbling, unable to reliably answer orientation questions

expectedActions.shortAction: Adenosine 6 mg IV rapid push via proximal site, immediately followed by 10 mL saline flush (fixed adult dose)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Adenosine 6 mg IV (proximal site) followed by 10 mL fluid bolus
expectedActions.rationale: First-line pharmacologic therapy for regular narrow-complex SVT.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply defibrillator/cardioversion pads; prepare synchronized cardioversion; consider sedation/analgesia for responsive patient
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Regular Narrow Complex Tachycardia – Unstable: Deliver a synchronized shock based on manufacturer's recommendations. For responsive patients, consider sedation and analgesia.
expectedActions.rationale: Given instability, cardioversion equipment and sedation should be readied in parallel rather than waiting for adenosine to fail.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and mental status after adenosine
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Full vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) with reassessment q 15 minutes or more frequently as appropriate
expectedActions.rationale: Frequent reassessment tracks response to therapy and guides next steps.

transitions.condition: Adenosine 6 mg IV is given without conversion; the SVT persists and the patient remains hypotensive and altered.

phases.name: Adenosine failed
phases.description: Adenosine failed to convert the rhythm; hemodynamic status continues to deteriorate. Crew proceeds to deliver synchronized cardioversion per the unstable pathway.
phases.triggerCondition: Despite adenosine 6 mg IV, SVT persists at HR 206 with worsening hypotension (BP 72/46) and declining mental status (GCS 10); crew proceeds directly to synchronized cardioversion per the Unstable SVT pathway.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, protecting own airway but minimally responsive
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Thready, barely palpable radial pulse; capillary refill >4 seconds

expectedActions.shortAction: Sedate per local sedation protocol prior to cardioversion (patient remains responsive to pain)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For responsive patients, consider sedation and analgesia.
expectedActions.rationale: The patient retains a pain response; procedural sedation should be attempted if it does not delay definitive treatment.

expectedActions.shortAction: Deliver synchronized cardioversion at manufacturer-recommended initial energy setting
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Deliver a synchronized shock based on manufacturer's recommendations.
expectedActions.rationale: Definitive treatment for unstable regular narrow-complex tachycardia unresponsive to adenosine.

expectedActions.shortAction: Document cardioversion time, synchronization, joules, and rhythm response; obtain monitor strip post-shock
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Cardioversion times, synchronization, attempts, joules, and response Obtain monitor strips after each intervention
expectedActions.rationale: Required documentation for the intervention and quality review.

transitions.condition: Synchronized cardioversion delivered; rhythm converts to sinus rhythm with rapid improvement in blood pressure and mental status.

Crew continues pharmacologic attempts (e.g., repeat adenosine or diltiazem) rather than delivering synchronized cardioversion despite persistent hypotension and altered mental status for more than 5 minutes.

phases.name: Converted to sinus rhythm
phases.description: Following synchronized cardioversion, the patient converts to sinus rhythm with prompt improvement in perfusion and mental status.
phases.triggerCondition: Immediately after synchronized cardioversion, the rhythm converts from SVT to sinus rhythm; heart rate, blood pressure, and mentation rapidly normalize.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Strong radial pulse; capillary refill <2 seconds
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Oh wow, that felt strange... I feel so much better now.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs, mental status, and 12-lead EKG post-conversion
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Full vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) with reassessment q 15 minutes or more frequently as appropriate
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms sustained conversion and hemodynamic stability prior to transport.

expectedActions.shortAction: Continue cardiac monitoring and transport; document rhythm changes throughout
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Initial rhythm and all rhythm changes
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing monitoring detects recurrence of SVT during transport.

phases.name: Cardioversion delayed
phases.description: Cardioversion is delayed while the crew continues pharmacologic attempts; the patient's perfusion continues to deteriorate toward hemodynamic collapse.
phases.triggerCondition: Rather than proceeding to synchronized cardioversion after failed adenosine, the crew administers additional AV-nodal blocking agents (e.g., diltiazem) and continues to reassess; more than 5 minutes elapse with the patient remaining hypotensive and altered, and perfusion continues to worsen toward hemodynamic collapse.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent but at risk given declining responsiveness
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Barely palpable central pulse only; capillary refill >4 seconds

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize ongoing decompensation; expedite synchronized cardioversion without further delay
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Regular Narrow Complex Tachycardia – Unstable: Deliver a synchronized shock based on manufacturer's recommendations.
expectedActions.rationale: Continued delay of cardioversion risks progression to cardiovascular collapse and cardiac arrest.
